summary: Puerto Ferro Light on Vieques was begun by Spain in 1896, lit under the United States in 1899, and abandoned in 1926. Its ruin lies in a national wildlife refuge.

light.characteristic: white flash every five seconds (early signature, per LighthouseFriends)

lens.note: Third-order Fresnel per LighthouseFriends and the U.S. Lighthouse Society record; EnciclopediaPR and Wikipedia give fifth order. Lantern removed later.

structures.note: Octagonal tower standing on a one-story dwelling. The U.S. Lighthouse Society record gives 38 ft from base to lantern centre and says the lantern is removed. LighthouseFriends says the lantern room is missing.
Keeper's quarters year 1896 in the U.S. Lighthouse Society record; construction began in 1896 under Spain (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Within the Vieques National Wildlife Refuge. The Puerto Ferro Trail (East), about 0.29 miles, is open year round. Much of the refuge is closed (LighthouseFriends; FWS). The ruin is not described as open inside.

facts.agency: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Vieques National Wildlife Refuge (FWS; LighthouseFriends).

events.note: Construction begun by the Spanish government; interrupted by the Spanish-American War (LighthouseFriends)
Activated for the first time in December 1899 (LighthouseFriends); the U.S. Lighthouse Society gives 1899 as the year established. EnciclopediaPR and Wikipedia give 1896.
Third-order Fresnel lens installed (U.S. Lighthouse Society)
The Light-House Board counts the completion of Puerto Ferro and Mona lights, bringing Puerto Rico's total to 15
Bottle paper found at the station on 17 November 1912 and forwarded by the keeper
Commissioner's estimate proposes to dismantle the station and rebuild at Port Real, about 3 miles west, using the same apparatus; estimate repeated in later years
Two earthquake shocks on 2 May; kitchen chimney cracked (LighthouseFriends)
Severe earthquake at 4.50 a.m. on 19 March; mercury thrown out, apparatus stopped until sunrise; old cracks enlarged and new cracks in the dwelling roof
Boarded up and abandoned (LighthouseFriends; EnciclopediaPR); the U.S. Lighthouse Society gives 1926 as the year discontinued
U.S. Navy expropriates two-thirds of Vieques, including the area around the light (LighthouseFriends; EnciclopediaPR gives the 1940s)
U.S. military ends its control of most of Vieques (LighthouseFriends)

corrections.why: The U.S. Lighthouse Society record and LighthouseFriends give 1899 (activated December 1899). EnciclopediaPR and Wikipedia give 1896 (the Spanish start). Proposed for human review; the sources disagree and the HAER report, which may settle it, was not read.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends and the U.S. Lighthouse Society record: third-order Fresnel. EnciclopediaPR and Wikipedia: fifth order (classed by its 12-mile range). The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: PROCESS BREACH: one direct fetch_text call was made to https://www.loc.gov/item/pr0045/ while looking for HAER PR-45; the guide says loc.gov is reached only through newspapers.py. It returned HTTP 403, no text was used, and no other loc.gov access was made for this station. NOT READ: HAER PR-45 (Murphy 1984), the best likely source for the first lighting and the lens, is hosted on loc.gov and was not read. The record's HAER PR-45 and Wikipedia's 'HAER No. PR-22' disagree; PR-45 is the record and EnciclopediaPR's citation. NOT READ: the 1979/1981 NRHP inventory (Nistal Moret, The Lighthouse System of Puerto Rico, 1846-1979) on docs.pr.gov returned an error, so the 1896 and 1899 dates and the lens order are not settled from it. First-lit conflict: 1896 (EnciclopediaPR, Wikipedia, lead only) against December 1899 (LighthouseFriends; U.S. Lighthouse Society 'year established 1899'). The 1900 Light-House Board report counts Puerto Ferro as complete by the year ended June 1900 (scan 83). The 1900 report's construction table (begun dates by light) is badly garbled in OCR; the names and years could not be matched by position with confidence, so it is not used. Keeper names: the archive roster prints Ramon Romero; the Bulletin's OCR prints 'R aimo n Romero' and LighthouseFriends prints Raimon. The story uses the roster spelling with the variant noted. Domingo Suarez Rosa is not on the archive roster. His Spanish-service stations include Port Ferro (Bulletin 1925 obituary); the Bulletin's 1924-1929 index lists him as keeper of Port Ferro (page 93). The years at Port Ferro are not stated, so the roster line has only the 1925 end date. The Commissioner's Port Real estimate was $34,000 in the 1915 volume and $40,000 from 1916 on; the story cites the later estimate printed at scan p. 580. The 1912 cistern request and the 1922 and 1925 earthquakes are from LighthouseFriends; the 1925 earthquake is confirmed in the Bulletin. The 1922 earthquake is LighthouseFriends only. The Navy dates: LighthouseFriends says 1941-1942; EnciclopediaPR says the 1940s. The story uses LighthouseFriends's dates. Wikipedia's lead says the light is open to the public and reached by gravel road; not used. Access: the FWS trail page is the access source. The lighthouse ruin is not described as open to enter. FACT-CHECK 2026-10-27: The Bulletin 1912 page image (PDF p. 47) reads 'Raimon Romero' (the OCR prints 'R aimo n'). The same page says the paper showed the bottle set adrift on 12 October 1907 about 240 miles east of Cape Henry, and that it was 'possible that it made a circuit of the North Atlantic' in five years; the story now attributes that wording to the Bulletin and the 'surmised' wording to LighthouseFriends. Port Real estimates: the 1915 report (scan p. 96, printed p. 91) gives $34,000; later estimates (scan p. 194, p. 293, p. 580, printed p. 82 and others) give $40,000 for 'Port Real, P. R., or East Point Vieques Island'. The story quotes the full phrase. The Bulletin 1925 PDF p. 22 confirms the earthquake wording; the death notice (PDF p. 36) confirms age 62 and 24 July. The 1924-1929 index (PDF p. 25) lists Domingo Suarez as keeper of Port Ferro, with no years. Ownership: LighthouseFriends says the U.S. Coast Guard owns the lighthouse; the FWS trail page covers access. The 'agency' field in facts describes the refuge, not the lighthouse owner. LighthouseFriends's visitor notes (sealed interior; climbing not safe) and its 1922 and 1925 accounts are paraphrased rather than quoted. The 1900 Board sentence counts the completion of Puerto Ferro and Mona lights; it gives no first-lit date, and the story says so. HAER PR-45 remains unread; the loc.gov fetch noted above was not repeated.
